---
title: Package a plugin
description: Make your application's hooks discoverable through a Python package.
sidebar:
  order: 1
---

Use a plugin to give the Bub app behavior you want to reuse or share. A Python package declares an entry point in the `bub` group; Bub imports that target and registers its hook implementations. You can also [reuse an existing plugin in your own service](/docs/build/reuse-plugins/) while keeping your host's entry point.

For a complete first example, follow [Write your first plugin](/docs/getting-started/first-plugin/). This guide covers the choices you make when packaging a plugin of your own.

Portable Agent Plugins use a different format: `plugin.json`, skills, and MCP servers. The [Agent Plugins integration](/docs/tutorials/agent-plugins/) loads those packages through a Python plugin.

## Declare an entry point

A plugin needs the application dependencies described in [Install Bub](/docs/getting-started/install/). Declare `bub[app]>=0.6.0` in the package dependencies for this guide. See [Upgrade to 0.6.0](/docs/reference/versions/) when updating an existing plugin.

```toml
[project.entry-points."bub"]
myplugin = "bub_myplugin.plugin"
```

The key `myplugin` identifies the plugin in diagnostics. The value names the Python object to import.

Choose one target form:

| Target | Registration | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bub_myplugin.plugin` | Register the module | Hooks are module-level functions |
| `bub_myplugin.plugin:plugin` | Register the instance | Hooks share state on an object |
| `bub_myplugin.plugin:MyPlugin` | Call the class or factory with `BubFramework`, then register its result | Hooks need the framework |

For the module form, define hooks at module level:

```python
from bub import hookimpl


@hookimpl
def build_prompt(message, session_id, state):
    return "Describe this workspace."
```

For the instance form, create the object in the target module:

```python
from bub import hookimpl


class MyPlugin:
    @hookimpl
    def build_prompt(self, message, session_id, state):
        return "Describe this workspace."


plugin = MyPlugin()
```

Every callable target receives the framework, including classes. Accept it in the constructor or factory:

```python
from bub import BubFramework, hookimpl


class MyPlugin:
    def __init__(self, framework: BubFramework) -> None:
        self.framework = framework

    @hookimpl
    def build_prompt(self, message, session_id, state):
        return f"Describe the workspace at {self.framework.workspace}."
```

These examples replace the prompt. Choose the hook for your actual task from [Change application behavior](/docs/build/hooks/).

## Register tools during import

If the package defines `@tool` functions, import their module from the entry-point module before an agent is created:

```python
from . import tools  # noqa: F401
```

The application takes a snapshot of registered tools when it creates a `BubAgent`. See [Add application tools](/docs/build/app-tools/) for registration, deferred loading, and code mode.

## Install into the application's environment

An editable install lets you change Python source without rebuilding the package. Use the same environment that runs Bub.

For a uv project, run from the plugin directory:

```bash
uv sync
uv run bub hooks
```

To install into an existing activated application environment, use `uv pip install -e .` and run `bub hooks` there.

`bub hooks` confirms registration. Check priority and return values by running the task your hook should handle. Bub registers builtin hooks before entry-point plugins. Hooks at equal priority generally run in reverse registration order; `tryfirst` and `trylast` affect that order. The [dispatch rules](/docs/reference/hooks/#iteration-order) explain which implementation runs first.

If the plugin is missing, check its entry-point group, the active environment, and startup logs for an import failure. Changes to package metadata require reinstalling the package.

## Share the plugin

Build and install a wheel into a separate environment before publishing it. Confirm that the entry point loads and that a representative task uses your hook. If you bundle skills or several plugins, follow [Package a Bub application](/docs/build/distribution/).
